# klms 0.2.0

This release adds a private, versioned course library to `klms`. It keeps a
local history of selected KLMS data so that notices, files, and local notes can
be searched and inspected without repeatedly fetching the same pages.

## Highlights

- `klms library sync` records courses, resources, notices, links, and optional
  downloaded file bytes. Subsequent commands can search the local collection,
  inspect changes and history, and show stable references.
- Downloaded files are deduplicated by SHA-256. `library content` provides a
  bounded preview, while `library export` writes the complete verified bytes
  without overwriting an existing file.
- Local summaries, notes, tags, and typed relationships are revisioned rather
  than updated in place. Retraction preserves their history.
- Notice extraction now records the post itself instead of surrounding page
  navigation and counters. Notice text and attachment recovery are presented
  separately when file bytes have not been downloaded.
- `klms spec` exposes the executable command grammar, and `klms completions`
  generates scripts for Bash, Elvish, Fish, PowerShell, and Zsh.
- `klms skill install` installs the matching companion Agent Skill embedded in
  the binary.

## Operational behavior

Library status distinguishes storage readiness from sync outcome and scope.
Partial, truncated, and unfinished attempts are reported explicitly; an
unfinished record does not claim that its original process is still running.
File downloads remain opt-in, and local-library operations never write to
KLMS or follow authenticated third-party links.

The machine-readable envelope is schema version 4. The local SQLite schema is
version 1 and remains experimental during the `0.x` series.

## Install

Prebuilt archives are available for Apple Silicon macOS and x86-64 Linux. Each
archive has a SHA-256 sidecar. The verified installer downloads the newest
release and installs both the binary and its companion skill:

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSLo install-klms.sh \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alazarteka/klms/main/scripts/install.sh
less install-klms.sh
bash install-klms.sh
```

Building from source requires Rust 1.86 or newer.

## Known limitation

`klms videos` currently exposes a Panopto LTI launcher, not the recordings
behind it. Recording discovery is tracked in
[issue #6](https://github.com/alazarteka/klms/issues/6).
